charts.title: Percentage of adults worldwide who stated select issues were the biggest health problems facing people in their country in 2023
charts.short: Leading health problems worldwide 2023
charts.description: A survey of people from 31 different countries around the world found that mental health was the biggest health problem respondents said was facing their country in 2023. Other health problems reported by respondents included cancer, stress, and obesity.
charts.note: Worldwide; July 21 to August 4, 2023; 23,274 respondents; 16-74 years; 31 countries
charts.source: Ipsos Percentage of respondents

charts.title: Percentage of adults worldwide who often thought about their own mental and physical wellbeing as of 2022
charts.short: Adults worldwide who often thought about their mental/physical wellbeing as of 2022
charts.description: In 2022, an average of around 70 precent of respondents from 34 countries around the world reported they very or fairly often thought about their own physical health. In comparison, around 58 percent of those surveyed reported very or fairy often thinking about their mental health. This statistic shows the percentage of adults worldwide who very or fairly often thought about their own mental/physical wellbeing as of 2022.
charts.note: Worldwide; July 22 to August 5, 2022; 23,507 respondents; 18 years and older; 34 countries
charts.source: Ipsos

charts.title: Average life expectancy at birth worldwide in 1990 and 2019, by region (in years)
charts.short: Life expectancy at birth worldwide by region 2019
charts.description: This statistic shows the average life expectancy worldwide in 1990 and 2019, sorted by WHO region. In 2019, a child born in the Americas could expect an average of 77.2 years to live, compared to 71 years in 1990.
charts.source: WHO

charts.title: Ranking of the 20 countries with the lowest life expectancy as of 2021
charts.short: Countries with the lowest life expectancy 2021
charts.description: The countries with the lowest life expectancy worldwide include the Chad, Nigeria, and Lesotho. As of 2021, people born in Chad could be expected to live only up to 53 years. This is almost 20 years shorter than the global life expectancy.
charts.source: Various sources (UN, Census reports from national offices,  Secretariat of the Pacific Community); World Bank Life expectancy in years

charts.title: Ranking of the 20 countries with the highest life expectancy as of 2021
charts.short: Countries with the highest life expectancy 2021
charts.description: As of 2021, the countries with the highest life expectancy included Japan, Liechtenstein, and South Korea. In Japan, a person could expect to live up to around 84 years. In general, the life expectancy for females is higher than that of males, with lifestyle choices and genetics the two major determining factors of life expectancy.
charts.source: Various sources (UN, Census reports from national offices,  Secretariat of the Pacific Community); World Bank Life expectancy in years

charts.title: Leading 20 countries based on adolescent fertility rate in 2021 (per 1,000 adolescent women)
charts.short: Countries with highest adolescent birth rate worldwide 2021
charts.description: In 2021, the birth rate for women aged 15 to 19 years in Niger was 170 per 1,000 women of that age, the highest adolescent birth rate of any country worldwide. This statistic shows the leading 20 countries based on adolescent birth rate in 2021, per 1,000 women aged 15 to 19 years.
charts.source: World Bank Adolescent birth rate per 1,000 women aged 15–19 years

charts.title: Prevalence of all types of stroke worldwide in 2019, by gender (in millions)
charts.short: Total stroke prevalence worldwide in 2019, by gender
charts.description: In 2019, the prevalence of stroke in women was higher than that of men. In total, there were over 101 million people who had experienced a stroke in 2019. This statistic shows the prevalence of all types of stroke worldwide in 2019, by gender.
charts.source: IHME

charts.title: Estimated number of diabetics worldwide in 2021, 2030, and 2045 (in millions)
charts.short: Diabetics worldwide 2021, 2030, and 2045
charts.description: The number of diabetics worldwide in 2021 was 537 million. That number is expected to grow until at least the year 2045. The projected number of diabetics is expected to reach 783 million by that time. With an increased number of diabetics, the prevalence of diabetes is also projected to increase to around 12 percent by 2045.
charts.source: International Diabetes Federation

charts.title: Percentage of diabetics in the global adult population in 2021, 2030, and 2045
charts.short: Diabetics prevalence worldwide 2021, 2030. and 2045
charts.description: Around 10.5 percent of the global adult population suffered from diabetes in 2021 - by the year 2045 this number is expected to rise to over 12 percent. Diabetes, or diabetes mellitus, refers to a group of metabolic disorders that result in chronic high blood sugar levels. Diabetes can lead to serious health complications, such as cardiovascular disease, chronic kidney disease, and stroke and is now among the top ten leading causes of death worldwide.
charts.source: International Diabetes Federation

charts.title: Diabetes prevalence by world region in 2021 and 2045*
charts.short: Prevalence of diabetes worldwide by region 2021 and 2045
charts.description: This statistic shows the world regions' age adjusted diabetes prevalence among adults (20-79 years) in 2021 and a 2045 forecast. In 2021, North America and the Caribbean had a 12 percent diabetes prevalence.
charts.note: Worldwide; 20-79 years; * All figures are age-adjusted estimates/forecasts. Read more
charts.source: International Diabetes Federation Age-adjusted prevalence

charts.title: Countries with the highest incidence rates of new HIV infections worldwide as of 2022 (per 1,000 population)
charts.short: Countries with the highest incidence rates of new HIV infections worldwide 2022
charts.description: In 2022, in South Africa there were around 3.15 HIV newly infected persons per every 1,000 inhabitants. This statistic depicts the countries with the highest incidence rates of new HIV infections worldwide as of 2022.
charts.source: UNAIDS HIV infections per 1,000 population

charts.title: HIV prevalence among the adult population in select countries worldwide as of 2022
charts.short: HIV prevalence in select countries worldwide 2022
charts.description: In 2022, some one percent of Thailand's population aged between 15 and 49 years was infected with HIV. This statistic describes the HIV prevalence among the adult population of select countries worldwide as of 2022.
charts.source: UNAIDS Percentage of population aged 15-49 years

charts.title: Leading 20 countries based on number of new malaria cases in 2021 (per 1,000 population at risk)
charts.short: Countries with the largest number of new malaria cases worldwide 2021
charts.description: In 2021, approximately 354 among one thousand inhabitants in Mali developed malaria. This statistic shows the 20 countries with the highest number of new malaria cases per 1,000 inhabitants at risk in 2021.
charts.source: World Bank Number of cases per 1,000 population at risk

charts.title: Incidence of tuberculosis worldwide in 2021, by region (per 100,000 population)
charts.short: Incidence of tuberculosis worldwide by region 2021
charts.description: In 2021, there were some 212 new cases of tuberculosis per 100,000 inhabitants in Africa. This statistic depicts the incidence of tuberculosis cases worldwide in 2021, distributed by WHO region.
charts.source: WHO Cases per 100,000 population

charts.title: Prevalence of treated end-stage renal disease in select countries worldwide in 2021 (per million population)
charts.short: Prevalence of treated end-stage renal disease in select countries worldwide 2021
charts.description: In 2021, Taiwan had around 3,839 cases of treated end-stage renal disease per one million population, compared to a rate of 1,445 per million population in Greece. This statistic shows the prevalence of treated end-stage renal disease in select countries worldwide in 2021.
charts.source: USRDS Number of treated cases per million population

charts.title: Percentage of adults worldwide who stated that mental health was the biggest health problem facing people in their country in 2023
charts.short: Adults worldwide who said mental health is their country's leading health issue 2023
charts.description: In 2023, around 67 percent of adults in Sweden stated that mental health was the biggest health problem facing people in their country, while in Japan only around 18 percent of adults stated the same. This statistic illustrates the percentage of adults worldwide who stated that mental health problems were the biggest health problems facing people in their country in 2023.
charts.note: Worldwide; July 22  to August 5, 2023; 23,507 respondents; 16-74 years; 34 countries
charts.source: Ipsos Percentage of respondents

charts.title: Percentage of adults worldwide who stated that stress was the biggest health problem facing people in their country in 2023
charts.short: Adults worldwide who stated that stress is their country's leading health issue 2023
charts.description: In 2023, around 39 percent of adults in Switzerland stated that they believed stress was the biggest health problem facing people in their country, while in the U.S. only around 18 percent of adults stated the same. This statistic illustrates the percentage of adults worldwide who stated that stress was the biggest health problem facing people in their country in 2023.
charts.note: Worldwide; July 21  to August 4, 2023; 23,274 respondents; 18 years and older; 31 countries
charts.source: Ipsos Percentage of respondents

charts.title: Leading countries worldwide based on stress experienced in the previous day in 2021-2022
charts.short: Most stressed countries worldwide in 2021-2022
charts.description: Surveys fielded in 2021 and 2022 in 122 countries around the world found that the countries in which people were most likely to state that they experienced stress in the previous day were Afghanistan, Lebanon, and Sierra Leone. In Afghanistan, around 68 percent of respondents reported feeling stressed in the day prior to being surveyed.
charts.note: Worldwide; 2021-2022; around 122,000; 18 years and older; 122 countries
charts.source: Gallup (Gallup Global Emotions Report)

charts.title: Percentage of the global population that suffers from select mental health or substance use disorders as of 2019
charts.short: Percentage of world population with select mental health disorders as of 2019
charts.description: This statistic depicts the percentage of the global population with select mental health and substance use disorders as of 2019. According to the data, almost four percent of the total global population suffered from an anxiety disorder.
charts.source: OWID

charts.title: Share of the population worldwide who suffered from anxiety disorders from 1990 to 2019
charts.short: Percentage of the population that had anxiety disorders worldwide from 1990 to 2019
charts.description: This statistic depicts the percentage of the population worldwide who had anxiety disorders from 1990 to 2019. According to the data, 3.94 percent of the population suffered from an anxiety disorder as of 2019.
charts.source: OWID Percentage of people

charts.title: Percentage of people worldwide who suffered from depression from 1990 to 2019
charts.short: Percentage of worldwide population that had depression from 1990 to 2019
charts.description: This statistic depicts the percentage of the population who had depression worldwide from 1990 to 2019. According the data, around 3.59 percent of the population worldwide had depression in 2019.
charts.source: OWID Percentage of people

charts.title: Share of the population who suffered from bipolar disorder worldwide from 1990 to 2019
charts.short: Percentage of the population with bipolar disorder worldwide from 1990 to 2019
charts.description: This statistic depicts the percentage of the world population who had bipolar disorder from 1990 to 2019. According to the data, the rate of bipolar disorder has remained relatively stable with around 0.51 percent of the population suffering each year.
charts.source: OWID Percentage of people

charts.title: Percentage of the population with schizophrenia worldwide from 1990 to 2019
charts.short: Share of the population with schizophrenia worldwide from 1990 to 2019
charts.description: This statistic depicts the share of the population who suffered from schizophrenia worldwide from 1990 to 2019. As of 2019, around 0.3 percent of the population had schizophrenia.
charts.source: OWID Percentage of the population

charts.title: Leading 20 countries based on suicide mortality rate in 2019 (per 100 000 population)
charts.short: Countries with the highest suicide mortality rates worldwide 2019
charts.description: The countries with the highest suicide mortality rate worldwide in 2019 included Lesotho, Guyana, and Eswatini. Suicide rates of men are much higher than among women in many countries. Lithuania has one of the highest suicide rates for men as of 2019, while South Korea reports the highest suicide rate for women.
charts.source: WHO Suicide mortality rate per 100 000 population

charts.title: Suicide rates in selected countries as of 2020, by gender (per 100,000 population)
charts.short: Number of suicides in selected countries by gender 2020
charts.description: South Korea currently has the highest overall suicide rate of any country worldwide. The suicide rate among women in South Korea is significantly higher than that of women in any other country. Nevertheless, suicide is commonly more prevalent among men than women.
charts.source: OECD Suicides per 100,000 population

charts.title: Percentage of respondents worldwide who took select steps to alleviate feelings of anxiety or depression as of 2020
charts.short: Respondents worldwide who took select steps to alleviate anxiety or depression, 2020
charts.description: In 2020, around 78 percent of respondents worldwide aged 15 years and older reported that they talked to friends or family to make themselves feel better when they had feelings of anxiety or depression. This statistic illustrates the percentage of respondents worldwide who took select steps to alleviate feelings of anxiety or depression as of 2020.
charts.note: Worldwide; 2020; over 119,000; 15 years and older; 113 countries
charts.source: Wellcome Trust Percentage of respondents
categories: Made a change to personal relationships
Made a change to work situation

charts.title: Global annual birth rate, death rate, and rate of natural population change from 1950 to 2021, with projections until 2100 (in deaths per 1,000 inhabitants)
charts.short: World: annual birth rate, death rate, and rate of natural population change 1950-2100
charts.description: The COVID-19 pandemic resulted in an increase in the global death rate, but had little to no significant impact on birth rates, causing population growth to dip slightly. On a global level, population growth is determined by the difference between the birth and death rate, and this is known as the rate of natural change - on a national or regional level, population change is also affected by migration.
charts.note: Worldwide; *Figures from 2022-2100 are estimates based on the UN's medium variant. Read more
charts.source: UN DESA

charts.title: Ranking of the 20 countries with the lowest death rates as of 2021 (per 1,000 people)*
charts.short: Countries with lowest death rates 2021
charts.description: In 2021, with just one death per one thousand people, Qatar was the country with the lowest death rate worldwide. This statistic shows a ranking of the 20 countries with the lowest death rates worldwide, as of 2021.
charts.source: World Bank Death rate per thousand people

charts.title: Ranking of the 20 countries with the highest death rates as of 2021 (per 1,000 people)*
charts.short: Countries with highest death rates 2021
charts.description: As of 2021, the countries with the highest death rates worldwide were Bulgaria, Serbia, and Ukraine. In these countries there were 19 to 22 deaths per 1,000 people. The country with the lowest death rate is Qatar, where there is just one death per 1,000 people.
charts.source: World Bank Death rate per thousand people

charts.title: Death rates in selected developed and developing countries as of 2021* (per 1,000 population)
charts.short: Death rates in select countries worldwide 2021
charts.description: As of 2021, with 17 deaths per every thousand of its population, Russia had the highest death rate among these select countries. This statistic represents a ranking of select developed and developing countries based on death rates as of 2021.
charts.source: World Bank Death rate per thousand people

charts.title: Leading causes of death worldwide in 2019 (in millions)
charts.short: Global death rate - leading causes 2019
charts.description: In 2019, the leading causes of death globally included ischemic heart disease, stroke and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). There were 8.89 million deaths from ischemic heart disease at that time and about 6.19 million deaths caused by stroke. In recent history, increases in life expectancy, increases in population and better standards of living have changed the leading causes of death over time.
charts.note: Worldwide; * Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease. Read more
charts.source: WHO Number of deaths in millions Causes of death

charts.title: Actual and public estimates of causes of death worldwide as of 2019*
charts.short: Public estimate vs. actual causes of death worldwide as of 2019
charts.description: According to the findings of a survey by IPSOS, worldwide people generally underestimate the proportion of deaths from cardiovascular diseases and cancer, two of the leading causes of death worldwide. It was found that on average respondents thought cardiovascular diseases accounted for just 11 percent of deaths worldwide, when in reality cardiovascular diseases account for 32 percent of deaths. This statistic shows the actual vs public estimates for causes of death worldwide as of 2019.
charts.note: Worldwide; November 22 to December 6, 2019; around 16,000; 16-74 years; * The main source of ‘actual’ data for causes of death around the world is the Institute for Health Metrics and Evaluation (IHME) Global Burden of Disease (GBD) [...] Read more
charts.source: Ipsos Percentage of all deaths
categories: Cardiovascular diseases such as heart disease
Lower respiratory infections such as pneumonia
Chronic respiratory diseases such as asthma

charts.title: Ranking of the 20 countries* with the highest infant mortality rate in 2023 (child deaths in the first year of life per thousand live births)
charts.short: Countries with the highest infant mortality rate 2023
charts.unit: child deaths in the first year of life per thousand live births
charts.description: This statistic shows the 20 countries* with the highest infant mortality rate in 2023. An estimated 103.06 infants per 1,000 live births died in the first year of life in Afghanistan in 2023.
charts.source: CIA Child deaths in the first year of life per 1,000 live births

charts.title: Ranking of the 20 countries* with the lowest infant mortality rate in 2023 (child deaths in the first year of life per 1,000 live births)
charts.short: Countries with the lowest infant mortality rate 2023
charts.unit: child deaths in the first year of life per 1,000 live births
charts.description: This statistic shows the 20 countries * with the lowest infant mortality rate in 2023. Estimated 1.51 out of 1,000 live births died in the first year of life in Slovenia in 2023.
charts.note: Worldwide; * States and territories. According to the source, all values are estimates. Read more
charts.source: CIA Child deaths in the first year of life per 1,000 live births

charts.title: Countries with the highest mortality rate among children aged under 5 as of 2021 (per 1,000 live births)
charts.short: Countries with highest mortality rate among children aged under five 2021
charts.description: In 2021, Niger had the highest mortality rate among children aged under five years, with an average of around 115 children dying, per one thousand live births, under five years of age. This statistic shows the countries with the highest mortality rate among children aged under five years as of 2021.
charts.source: WHO Deaths per thousand live births

charts.title: Annual number of deaths from select risk factors worldwide in 2019 (in millions)
charts.short: Number of deaths worldwide from select risk factors in 2019
charts.description: In 2019, high blood pressure contributed to around 10.85 million deaths worldwide, while there were around 5.02 million deaths due to obesity. This statistic shows the annual number of deaths from select risk factors worldwide in 2019.
charts.source: IHME (GBD); OWID Number of deaths in millions

charts.title: Countries with the highest prevalence of daily smokers worldwide as of 2019
charts.short: Countries with the highest share of daily smokers worldwide in 2019
charts.description: As of 2019, around 33 percent of individuals aged 15 years and older in Serbia were daily tobacco smokers. In the same year, 28 percent of individuals in France were also daily smokers. This statistic illustrates the 20 countries with the highest prevalence of daily smokers worldwide as of 2019.
charts.source: University of Illinois Chicago; Vital Strategies; WHO Prevalence of daily smokers

charts.title: Countries with the highest per capita consumption of alcohol in 2019 (in liters of pure alcohol per year)
charts.short: Countries with highest per capita consumption of alcohol 2019
charts.unit: liters of pure alcohol per year
charts.description: The countries with the highest per capita consumption of alcohol include Czechia, Latvia, and the Republic of Moldova. Laws regarding the production, sale and consumption of alcohol differ by region and country but alcohol is one of the most widely used drugs worldwide. Abuse of alcohol has been linked to a number of short-term and long-term negative health effects.
charts.source: WHO Liters of pure alcohol per capita per year

charts.title: Prevalence of obesity among adults in selected countries as of 2021, or latest year available, by gender*
charts.short: Obesity - prevalence in selected countries by gender 2021
charts.description: In 2021, over 30 percent of both men and women in the United States reported themselves as obese (BMI over 30), making it the country with the highest percentage of obese adults on this list. Other selected countries on the list with a high prevalence of obesity among adults included Iceland and Russia.
charts.source: OECD Share of the adult population

charts.title: Percentage of deaths attributed to obesity in select countries worldwide in 2019*
charts.short: Share of deaths in select countries worldwide attributed to obesity in 2019
charts.description: In 2019, around 22 percent of deaths in Bahrain were attributed to obesity, while around 13 percent of deaths in the United States were attributed to obesity. This statistic shows the percentage of deaths in select countries worldwide that were attributed to obesity in 2019.
charts.note: Worldwide; 2019; * Obesity is defined as having a body-mass index (BMI) equal to or greater than 30. BMI is a person'sweight in kilograms divided by their height in meters squared. Shown is the share of total deaths, fromany cause, with [...] Read more
charts.source: IHME (GBD); OWID Percentage of deaths

charts.title: Percentage of illicit drug use in global population in 2021, by drug type
charts.short: Global population share of illicit drug use 2021, by drug
charts.description: Worldwide, it is estimated that 0.72 to 1.49 percent of the global population between 15 and 64 years of age have used opioids in the past year, while approximately 0.57 to 0.86 percent have used amphetamines. This statistic shows the estimated percentage of the global population that have used illicit drugs in the past year as of 2021, by drug type.
charts.source: UNODC

charts.title: Global estimated number of people who inject drugs as of 2021, by region
charts.short: Global number of people who inject drugs as of 2021, by region
charts.description: In 2021, it was estimated that around 3.41 million people in North America were currently injecting drugs. This statistic shows the estimated number of the general population that currently injects drugs as of 2021, by world region.
charts.source: UNODC; WHO; World Bank Number of people who inject drugs

charts.title: Countries with the highest share of domestic governmental health expenditure in 2020*
charts.short: Countries with highest government health expenditure share 2020
charts.description: This statistic describes the countries with the highest share of domestic governmental health expenditure in 2020. In this year, Costa Rica had the highest percentage, spending about 25 percent of its total governmental expenditures on health-related issues.
charts.note: Worldwide; 2020; * As a percentage of general government expenditure. Read more
charts.source: WHO Percentage of total governmental expenditure

charts.title: Health expenditure as a percentage of gross domestic product (GDP) in selected countries in 2022
charts.short: Health expenditure as a percentage of GDP in select countries 2022
charts.description: Among OECD member countries, the United States had the highest percentage of gross domestic product spent on health care in 2022. The U.S. spent nearly 16 percent of its GDP on health care services. Germany, France and Japan followed the U.S. with distinctly smaller percentages. The United States had both significantly higher private and public spending on health compared with other developed countries.
charts.source: OECD Percentage of gross domestic product

charts.title: Per capita health expenditure in selected countries in 2022 (in U.S. dollars)
charts.short: Per capita health expenditure in selected countries 2022
charts.description: In 2022, the United States had the highest per capita health expenditure among OECD countries. At that time, per capita health expenditure in the U.S. amounted to 12,555 U.S. dollars, significantly higher than in Switzerland, the country with the second highest per capita health expenditure. Germany, Norway, and the Netherlands are also within the top five countries with the highest per capita health expenditure. The United States also spent the highest share of it’s gross domestic [...]
charts.source: OECD Per capita expenditure in current PPPs

charts.title: Countries with the lowest share of governmental health expenditure in 2020*
charts.short: Countries with lowest governmental health expenditure 2020
charts.description: This statistic depicts the countries with the lowest share of government health expenditure in 2020. In that year, South Sudan had the lowest health expenditure worldwide, measured by the percentage of total governmental expenditures. Only 2.1 percent of all expenditures went to health-related issues.
charts.note: Worldwide; 2020; * As a percentage of general government expenditure. Read more
charts.source: WHO Percentage of general government expenditure

charts.title: Global spending on medicines in 2010, 2022, and a forecast for 2027 (in billion U.S. dollars)
charts.short: Global spending on medicines 2010-2027
charts.description: Global spending on medicine continues to grow. In 2022, approximately 1.48 trillion U.S. dollars had been spent on medicines, up from just 887 billion U.S. dollars in 2010. That number is expected to increase to over 1.9 trillion by the year 2027. Spending on medicines has increased everywhere globally. However, the United States takes the lead in total medicines spending globally and is expected to remain the top country for medicines spending through 2027.
charts.source: IQVIA

charts.title: Projected spending on medicine of selected countries worldwide in 2026 (in billion U.S. dollars)
charts.short: Country comparison in spending on medicine 2026
charts.description: In 2026, the United States is projected to spend between 685 and 715 billion U.S. dollars on medicine. Estimates for the United States are much higher than those of other countries on the list. For the same year, Germany’s expected expenditure estimates were between 76 and 96 billion U.S. dollars.
charts.source: IQVIA Spending in billion U.S. dollars

charts.title: Global oncology spending from 2013 to 2024 (in billion U.S. dollars)
charts.short: Global oncology spending 2013-2024
charts.description: This statistic shows total oncology spending worldwide, including spending for supportive care, from 2013 to 2024. In 2022, global oncology spending totaled 193 billion U.S. dollars. In comparison, costs stood at 90 billion dollars six years earlier.
charts.source: IQVIA

charts.title: Top 10 countries based on diabetes health expenditure in 2021 (in billion U.S. dollars)
charts.short: Diabetes health expenditure top 10 countries in 2021
charts.description: This statistic shows the top 10 countries based on diabetes-related health expenditure in 2021. The health expenditure in the U.S. is the highest with almost 380 billion U.S. dollars, followed by China with 165 billion U.S. dollars.
charts.source: International Diabetes Federation Expenditure in billion U.S. dollars
